instead of "success metric"

consider a "time to pivot / cancel metric"

what signal would persuade the team to pivot immediately?

"success" tells us nothing, really. keep going? celebrate? do more?

That's blasphemy say some.

That's incredible, say others.

IME, you tend to see this practice when the following pieces of the puzzle are in place:
imagine if product managers needed to get their strategy PRs reviewed

Why does our documentation suck?

Why can't I find the document I need NOW?
OH: The wiki is like a fridge. People can't find anything, so they keep buying more food. More food makes it harder to find things. And when they do it is rotting.
I'm getting the distinct impression that the "projects to products" shift in many big companies is more like a "project factory to feature factory" shift.

A big reason why I think people avoid talking to customers is fear.

Fear of being “even more confused”

Fear of “casting doubt on the project”

Fear “people will challenge the sample size”

Fear they “mess up the interview”

Fear of “slowing things down”
